org.name: His Majesty's Prison and Probation Service

hazard: Lack of knowledge about emergency response codes

concerns.quote: The first reception nurse who saw Mr Williams when he entered HMP Pentonville gave evidence that he had no thoughts of self harm or suicide, but she recorded that he had. It appears she may benefit from additional training and/or supervision. . There was no second reception screen conducted. If Mr Williams was not brought to healthcare staff for his second reception screen then healthcare staff needed to follow this up. . The first reception nurse did not make the referral to the mental health team
concerns.hazard: lack of proper reception screening and mental health referral

concerns.quote: Mr Williams said to several members of staff that he would self harm or hang himself if he wanted something done and it was not happening quickly enough (rather than because he actually wanted to die.) This was recorded on his assessment, care in custody, teamwork (ACCT) document. Some prison officers did not seem familiar with the very important contents of the ACCT, not even the inside cover. concerns.hazard: inadequate understanding of ACCT protocol and risk documentation

concerns.quote: The issue of the difference between a code blue and a code red is one about which | have written before. One senior prison officer said in evidence that if she did not know the difference between a code blue and a code red, then there would be some serious concerns. She did not. She had been given a small card describing code blue and code red (a card which another officer kept about her person and even produced from the witness box), and she still retained that card. concerns.hazard: lack of knowledge about emergency response codes

concerns.quote: The prison officers did not have even the most basic first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training. | am aware from other inquests that this is not provided at a national level. | have written about this before. It seems a significant gap, even allowing for the fact that there are always two trained nurses on site.
concerns.hazard: absence of basic emergency medical training among prison officers

reports.title: Luke Pearce: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: relevant training and guidance to equip staff to understand when and how to enter a cell in a medical emergency, and the appropriate use of Code Blue and Code Red communications in a medical emergency
concerns.hazard: delayed staff training on cell entry and emergency communications

links.explanation: Both reports highlight insufficient staff understanding of when to use Code Blue versus Code Red communications during medical emergencies. The later report expands the concern to include timely training on entering cells, while the earlier focuses specifically on officers not knowing the code difference.
